title: DEPARK December Bulletin
excerpt: DEPARK's December newsletter presents the latest developments in technology development zones, events, and up-to-date news for companies, all in one place.
author: Siskon Basın
content:
Siskon Automation and Software participated in the TÜSİAD SD2 2019 Digital Transformation in Industry Program. This program aims to strengthen the industrial digital transformation process and support the digital technology supplier ecosystem by connecting those who utilize digital technologies in production processes with providers of digital technology solutions; it promotes the capabilities of digital technology suppliers and fosters technology production, while showcasing best-practice examples that inspire digital transformation planning. As the first comprehensive program dedicated to digital transformation in industry, TÜSİAD SD2 brought together 18 industry-leading technology-using companies with SME-scale technology suppliers in 2019.

Following the application and preliminary screening stages of TÜSİAD SD2, the 18 technology-using companies and the shortlisted micro, small, and medium-sized technology suppliers convened in September for the Technology Integration Program (STEP). During the STEP event, matches were established between the technology-using companies and the technology suppliers that had passed the preliminary screening. These matched pairs will collaborate in the coming period to prepare solution proposals. The success stories resulting from this process will be shared with the public at the "Digital Transformation in Industry Success Stories Ceremony" to be held at the end of the year. Siskon Automation and Software, a DEPARK-based company, was selected as the technology provider for Kordsa’s project titled “Autonomous Tool/Product Mounting and Dismounting System” within the scope of the TÜSİAD SD2 2019 Digital Transformation in Industry program. Having reached the finals among more than 500 technology development companies in the 2018 TÜSİAD SD2 program, Siskon Automation and Software had previously been chosen by Yaşar Holding as the technology firm for its project in the “Data Collection and Monitoring Systems” category.

title: TÜSİAD SD2 Digital Transformation in Industry Program 2019
excerpt: TÜSİAD's Digital Transformation in Industry Program offers comprehensive training and consultancy support to prepare Turkish industrial companies for Industry 4.0.
author: Siskon Basın
content:
TÜSİAD SD2, the first comprehensive program focused on digital transformation in industry, brought together 18 leading technology-user companies with SME-scale technology suppliers.

Companies matched through the program will collaborate to develop joint solution projects. The success stories emerging from the program will be shared with the public during the “Digital Transformation in Industry Success Stories Ceremony” to be held at the end of the year.

The second year of TÜSİAD SD2, launched by the Turkish Industry and Business Association (TÜSİAD) to support digital transformation in industry, is currently underway. Organized with Vodafone Business as the Gold Sponsor, Inventram as the Silver Sponsor, and Gün+Partners as the Legal Support Partner, the program aims to connect technology-user companies seeking digital transformation with the right solution providers. At the same time, it offers technology suppliers developing innovative products and services a platform where they can present their solutions and validate them with potential customers.

Following the application and preliminary evaluation stages of TÜSİAD SD2, 18 technology-user companies met with shortlisted micro, small, and medium-sized technology suppliers at the Industry-Technology Integration Program (STEP) held on September 10. During the STEP event, technology-user companies and supplier companies that passed the preliminary evaluation process were matched with one another.

The companies matched through STEP will work together in the coming months to prepare solution projects. The resulting success stories will be presented to the public at the “Digital Transformation in Industry Success Stories Ceremony” to be held at the end of the year. The event also featured panel discussions led by industry experts on topics ranging from public support programs to digital transformation tools.

The opening speech of the event was delivered by TÜSİAD Vice Chairman and Chairman of the Industry Policies Round Table, Bahadır Balkır. Emphasizing that decision-makers are increasingly facing uncertainties in the era of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, Balkır stated:

“Last year, we launched the TÜSİAD SD2 Program in response to these challenges. During the pilot year, we brought together 13 leading industrial companies and 14 technology suppliers, creating collaboration opportunities that contributed to the development of Türkiye’s innovation ecosystem. This year, we are bringing together 18 leading technology-user companies with valuable technology producers from across the country.”

Following Bahadır Balkır, TÜSİAD Chairman Simone Kaslowski took the stage and highlighted that the increasingly competitive environment driven by digital transformation creates constant pressure for innovation.

“New technologies are creating an environment in many industries where the winner takes all. This makes success more important than ever. In such an environment, collaboration between companies, governments, universities, and other stakeholders plays a critical role in the competitiveness of both countries and businesses.”

Kaslowski also emphasized that success in digital transformation requires new leadership and management capabilities:

“The quality and value of production are now measured not only by average internet speed and the number of collaborative robots per thousand employees, but also by STEM competencies, employee training, data security regulations, logistics performance, infrastructure quality, carbon emissions, and recycling rates. Developments such as 3D technologies, advanced materials, and gene-editing technologies are increasingly blurring the boundaries between the digital and physical worlds. The TÜSİAD SD2 Program provides a valuable opportunity to approach digital transformation from a holistic perspective. It is encouraging to see the program, which began as a pilot initiative last year, continuing this year with increased participation.”

Another speaker at the event, TÜSİAD SD2 Task Force Chair Perihan İnci, provided information about the program’s processes. She stated that TÜSİAD SD2 was developed as a platform designed to bring technology-user companies together with technology suppliers.

Perihan İnci noted that the program contributes significantly to strengthening the ecosystem of technology users and suppliers, addressing the needs of technology users, supporting technology production by SMEs, and creating successful examples of digital transformation practices.

Following the matchmaking sessions, TÜSİAD Chairman Simone Kaslowski delivered the closing remarks:

“As of today, a one-to-one collaboration period begins for some of our companies with their technology-user partners. It will be a long and demanding process, but also an extremely valuable and exciting one. I would like to underline once again that there are no winners or losers in this program. Technology suppliers who were not matched are now an inseparable part of this network. I believe this program has created the spark that Turkish industry needs. I sincerely believe that we will hear many inspiring success stories in the coming period.”

title: Automation in logistics is being discussed.
excerpt: How automation technologies drive efficiency gains and transform the supply chain in the logistics sector remains a key topic on the industry's agenda.
author: Siskon Basın
content:
The 7th Automation Technologies in Logistics Seminar, organized by Sick in cooperation with LODER, has just started at Istanbul Marriott Hotel Asia.

The event, organized by Sick and LODER with broad participation, began with speeches by Sick Türkiye General Manager Mehmet Kahveci and LODER Chairman of the Board Prof. Dr. Mehmet Tanyaş. Throughout the day, presentations will be delivered by LODER, Aras Kargo, Sick, SEW, Siskon, Berrmak, Tunaylar, and Dijitalis. In the afternoon session, Prof. Dr. Özgür Demirtaş will give a speech. The 7th Automation Technologies in Logistics Seminar is being held with the participation of more than 350 guests.

With more than 70 years of experience and over 8,800 employees worldwide, Sick is recognized as one of the world's leading sensor manufacturers, offering the broadest range of products and technologies in the sensor industry. Its areas of expertise are as follows:

FACTORY AUTOMATION

The Factory Automation division encompasses all sensor-related tasks required for automated production within a factory. The goal is to count, classify, position, recognize object shapes, and determine positional information at every stage of production. In addition, industrial safety solutions are provided for factories.

LOGISTICS AUTOMATION

The Logistics Automation division serves the design and optimization of logistics and distribution processes. Wherever material flow needs to be automated, or wherever sorting, identification, and storage operations need to be more efficient, faster, and more reliable, Sick's Logistics Automation division provides the best possible solutions.

PROCESS AUTOMATION

The Process Automation division includes gas and dust analysis systems, flow measurement systems, and gas and dust sensors for tunnel ventilation control in industrial facilities. The objective is both to increase efficiency through continuous monitoring and measurements at every stage of the process and to provide environmentally conscious and reliable solutions that comply with regulations regarding gas and dust emission measurements.

title: Siskon Showcased Its Digital Solutions for the Tobacco Industry at InterSupply 2026
author: Siskon Basın
content:
Siskon participated in InterSupply 2026, one of the leading international meeting points for the tobacco industry. Held at Messe Dortmund in Dortmund, Germany, from September 15–17, 2026, the exhibition brought together tobacco manufacturers, technology providers, and industry professionals from around the world. Siskon welcomed visitors at Stand 3.F03 in Hall 3.

As tobacco manufacturing becomes increasingly connected, intelligent, and data-driven, Siskon continues to develop solutions that address the industry's needs for connectivity, traceability, efficiency, and operational visibility by combining its expertise in industrial automation, software, and manufacturing technologies.

One of the solutions highlighted by Siskon during the exhibition was Tobacco Machine Communication (TMC). TMC is an OPC UA-based standard jointly developed by the OPC Foundation and a working group of tobacco manufacturers. The standard aims to unify fragmented machine communications caused by different protocols and data formats under a common information model within tobacco production facilities. Through its TMC solution, Siskon aims to bridge the gap between machines, systems, and people while delivering measurable value through connected automation and data-driven manufacturing technologies.

Throughout the exhibition, the Siskon team shared its expertise in digital transformation and software solutions for tobacco manufacturing. Discussions focused on industrial communication, automation, and traceability challenges, creating opportunities for future collaborations and partnerships.

Learn more about the TMC solution: https://opcuatmc.com

title: Real-Time Machine Monitoring Solution
excerpt: Uninterrupted Transparency in Production: Real-Time Machine Monitoring and Performance Management
author: Siskon Mühendislik
content:
Monitoring and analysis of production data for effective, data-driven decisions

In the era of digital transformation, data is no longer merely something to be observed; it is the most valuable asset for decision-making. Designed to optimize and streamline production processes, Monitora by Siskon empowers manufacturers to lead the digital transformation by making every stage of production traceable, analyzable, and manageable. By collecting real-time data from industrial machinery and processes, Monitora enables businesses to monitor production performance instantly, detect deviations, and identify areas for improvement. Its user-friendly interface and flexible architecture support rapid, effective decision-making by transforming field data into actionable insights.

Support for management and shop-floor operators
Real-time data collection enables the monitoring of all machines, stations, and processes across the production line. Direct integration with PLCs and control systems from various brands is supported. Time- and event-based data logging facilitates root cause analysis and performance benchmarking, allowing for the rapid elimination of recurring issues. Trend analysis of process data can be used to optimize and proactively shape maintenance schedules and quality strategies. Monitora integrates seamlessly with existing systems, eliminating the need for additional investments or lengthy implementation processes. Based on open, secure, and standards-compliant communication via OPC UA, the solution offers a web-based, multilingual user interface with live monitoring dashboards, as well as role-based user management and authorization. Alarm monitoring and management features include support for email and SMS notification systems. A robust analytical foundation, flexible integration capabilities, and streamlined design add value for both management and shop-floor operators.

title: The impact of the Izmir Agricultural Technology Center will not be limited to Izmir.
excerpt: The Izmir Agricultural Technology Center aims to become a hub for innovative solutions—not only at the regional but also at the national level—by accelerating digital transformation in the agricultural sector.
author: Siskon Basın
content:
Noting that the İzmir Agricultural Technology Center (İTTM) is expected to become operational in the first quarter of 2024, İzmir Commodity Exchange (İTB) Secretary General Dr. Erçin Güdücü stated that the center will also make it possible to develop technologies addressing different needs in different regions of Türkiye, a major agricultural producer.

The establishment works of the İzmir Agricultural Technology Center (İTTM), which combines agriculture with technology and has been initiated under the leadership of the İzmir Commodity Exchange (İTB) in partnership with universities and public institutions in the city, have reached the final stage.

Having been involved in the project from day one and promoting İTTM and its advantages to entrepreneurs at every meeting and trade fair he attended both in Türkiye and abroad, İTB Secretary General Dr. Erçin Güdücü emphasized that the impact of agricultural technologies developed there would not be limited to İzmir. Dr. Güdücü said, “Türkiye is an important agricultural producer. At our center, it will also be possible to develop technologies tailored to different needs in different regions of our country. New production methods, localized technologies, and new cost-reducing products and services developed here will support the enhancement of our agricultural sector’s global competitiveness.”

Stating that the construction of the İTTM service building in Menemen is continuing, Dr. Güdücü said, “We are carrying out our final checks to ensure that the physical infrastructure needs of İTTM stakeholders are fully met. Unless we encounter any major setbacks, we will take delivery of the building within a few weeks and organize details such as shared-area furniture, internet infrastructure, and security systems. At the same time, the selection process for the start-ups that will conduct research and development activities at İTTM will be completed. Afterwards, İTTM will be ready for operation. Our expectation is that İTTM will become operational during the first quarter of 2024.”

Stating that the system they are developing enables matchmaking among stakeholder groups with different needs, Dr. Güdücü said, “We are working on a system through which entrepreneurs, companies, agricultural producers, agricultural machinery and equipment manufacturers, agricultural processors, researchers, and agricultural engineers that we meet at events organized together with various stakeholders can be classified according to stakeholder profiles, technology fields they use, and agricultural products they work with.”

Providing opportunities for testing under real-life conditions

Güdücü noted that thanks to the laboratories and equipment within İTTM, entrepreneurs can focus their financial resources on developing solutions rather than infrastructure investments. “From the entrepreneurs’ perspective, İTTM supports the development and commercialization of agricultural technologies by providing the physical environment, infrastructure, and business connections required for information technology-based R&D activities in the agricultural sector. Furthermore, due to its TEKMER status, entrepreneurs within the center can benefit from various tax incentives and support mechanisms provided under Law No. 5746 on Supporting Research, Development and Design Activities. Beyond these advantages, the center offers agricultural lands and application areas, enabling developed technologies to be tested under real-life conditions, on real products, and with real users. This helps entrepreneurs evaluate the effectiveness and real-world performance of their products in agricultural applications and make the necessary improvements.”

Remote membership model also available

Stating that İTTM aims to develop agricultural technologies together with the private sector, public institutions, researchers, and agricultural producers and processors who are the users of these solutions, Dr. Güdücü said, “In addition to entrepreneurs and businesses with technology-oriented ideas/projects involving R&D and product/process/service innovation focused on information technologies in agriculture, companies that can provide R&D support services, researchers, agricultural producers, and agricultural machinery manufacturers can also be part of our center. To address the different needs of companies, we offer private offices, open offices with dedicated desks, and open offices with shared desks. Finally, we also have a remote membership model that allows stakeholders interested in agricultural technologies but located far from İTTM to become part of the ecosystem and benefit from training, consultancy, networking, and similar activities.”

title: Bakırçay University Students Organized a Technical Visit to Siskon
excerpt: Bakırçay University students visited Siskon Otomasyon ve Yazılım A.Ş. as part of a technical trip and gained insights into industrial automation and digital transformation processes.
author: Siskon İnsan Kaynakları
content:
Our Computer Programming Department organized a technical visit to Siskon Automation and Software Inc. Students who participated in the visit had the opportunity to learn about innovations and technologies in the industry. The company's General Manager, Muvaffak Amasya, delivered a comprehensive presentation on Siskon Automation's activities in factory automation and process control technologies.

Muvaffak Amasya explained the achievements Siskon Automation has accomplished since its establishment and its goals for the future. He provided detailed information about technologies used in factory automation, software solutions, and process control systems. By also sharing insights into the company's vision, mission, and values, he became a source of inspiration for our students.

Following this, Human Resources Chief Selma Çakır informed students about internship and recruitment processes within the company. The application stages, interview processes, and recruitment criteria were shared in detail. Students were provided with valuable insights regarding career opportunities at Siskon Automation.

Burçin Erdoğan Özhun, who serves as Senior Operation Lead at the company, spoke about daily work routines, projects, and challenges encountered in professional life. Information was provided about software development processes, as well as the tools and technologies used. In addition, she emphasized the importance of teamwork and continuous learning. Students had the opportunity to observe firsthand how a professional software development environment operates.

Following the presentations, a question-and-answer session was held with the participation of Deputy General Manager Aslı Amasya and Human Resources Assistant Gamze Dağlı. Students had the opportunity to ask questions about topics they were curious about. Company representatives answered the students' questions and provided guidance. Afterwards, students toured the company and held one-on-one discussions with other software developers. In this way, they gained valuable experiences both technically and socially.

This technical visit was highly productive in enhancing our students' industry knowledge and experience. Thanks to the hospitality of Siskon Automation and Software Inc. and the valuable information shared, our students received important guidance for planning their future careers. We would like to thank Siskon Automation and Software Inc.

title: Siskon Automation SCADA Applications
excerpt: The SCADA solutions developed by Siskon elevate real-time monitoring, data acquisition, and process control in manufacturing facilities to a higher level.
author: Siskon Basın
content:
Siskon Automation SCADA Applications

Siskon Automation has been developing HMI and SCADA software solutions since 2001. The company is the Türkiye representative and distributor of Copa-Data's SCADA software solutions. Siskon Automation has successfully delivered numerous projects in Türkiye using the Zenon SCADA platform developed by Copa-Data. In addition, through its own SCADA software developed in C#, the company can provide more flexible and customer-oriented solutions whenever required. Depending on project requirements, Siskon Automation is also capable of implementing solutions using other SCADA platforms.

In line with customer requirements, Siskon Automation implemented an automation solution for a fully automated beer production facility using the Genesis Iconics SCADA platform. Furthermore, with its in-house SCADA software developed in C#, the company has completed automation projects for numerous tobacco machinery systems, painting machines, pharmaceutical production facilities, and textile machines. In the brewery automation application, the entire system can be monitored and controlled simultaneously from a central computer through Genesis Iconics SCADA. The Siemens S7-415 PLC communicates with the Genesis Iconics SCADA system via the Siemens OPC Server using the Profibus protocol. Data collected from production lines is stored in a Microsoft Access database. Once process parameters are configured on the central computer, the system operates fully automatically. Authorized users are also provided with the ability to manually intervene in the system whenever modifications are required. Target tank temperatures can be adjusted from the central computer, and all reports can be displayed in tabular or graphical formats.

In another application, monitoring machine connections, alarm management, and compliance visualization for tobacco machinery were achieved using a SCADA system developed in C# together with Beckhoff PLCs. Communication between the Beckhoff OPC Server, SCADA system, and PLCs is performed via the Ethernet protocol. SQL Server was used as the database platform. In addition, the software developed in C# enables system monitoring across the entire intranet without requiring the installation of additional programs, while authorized users are allowed to manage and control the system remotely.

For textile machine projects, all machine connections and components were visualized within the C#-based SCADA application, offering comprehensive monitoring and control capabilities. Initially designed using Monitrol MII operator panels and RIO input/output units, the textile machine SCADA system was later modernized with touchscreen Siskon IPC industrial computers, Beckhoff PLCs, and a new, more advanced visual SCADA interface.

Relying on the high performance of Siskon touchscreen industrial computers, critical systems such as pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities have also been controlled using these industrial computers, Beckhoff PLCs, and custom-developed C# SCADA software. All collected data is securely stored within SQL databases to ensure maximum reliability and data security.

The PLCs, SCADA platforms, and database systems used in each project are selected entirely according to customer requirements. Solutions can also be implemented using different PLC brands and SCADA software packages depending on project needs. The use of SQL databases further supports future expansion and development opportunities.

Although Siskon Automation generally utilizes Beckhoff PLCs, Zenon SCADA, SQL Server databases, and TwinCAT OPC Server technologies in its automation projects, the company also develops turnkey solutions using alternative PLCs, custom C#-based SCADA systems, and Access or Oracle databases according to customer demands, as demonstrated in the examples above.

title: Galaksiya’s Spin-off, Time Reactor, Receives Investment from Siskon at a $2 Million Valuation
excerpt: Time Reactor received an investment from Siskon Industrial Automation and Software at a valuation of $2 million.
author: Siskon Basın
content:
Time Reactor, a spin-off of Galaksiya, has secured an investment from Siskon Industrial Automation and Software at a valuation of $2 million.

This investment aims to enable Time Reactor to bring its predictive maintenance and predictive quality solutions to a broader industrial ecosystem and to strengthen its position in both the Turkish and global markets. Furthermore, the initiative seeks to promote the adoption of AI-driven data analytics solutions in the industry, boost efficiency in production processes, reduce error rates, and facilitate industrial enterprises' access to predictive maintenance technologies.

Tayfun Gökmen Halaç, CTO of Time Reactor, stated that they began their work two years ago after identifying a need for AI solutions tailored to time-series data and developed deep neural networks through a TÜBİTAK-supported project. He noted that upon realizing their research had moved beyond the realm of academic study, they decided to transform this technology into a standalone product.

Erdem Eser Ekinci, Co-founder of Galaksiya Information Technologies, remarked that thanks to generative AI, machines would evolve from mere data-generating systems into autonomous entities capable of providing insights into the future. He emphasized that Time Reactor empowers businesses with predictability through big data analytics and AI technologies.

Muvaffak Amasya, Co-founder of Siskon Industrial Automation and Software, stated that data analysis in production processes can now be conducted with a focus on the future, rather than just the past. Stating that AI solutions like Time Reactor represent the future of industrial automation, Amasya noted that with this investment, they are ushering in a new era in the sector by combining Siskon's experience in production processes with Time Reactor's AI vision.

**Source:** Time Reactor, a Galaksiya spin-off, receives investment from Siskon at a $2 million valuation – Webrazzi

title: Siskon Joins the Horizon Europe Industry 2026 Brokerage Platform
author: Siskon Basın
content:
Siskon has joined the Horizon Europe Industry 2026 Brokerage Platform, established under the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation framework programme. The platform aims to foster partnerships for Cluster 4 (Digital, Industry and Space) calls by bringing together research institutions, universities, industrial organizations, and technology providers from across Europe.

On the platform, Siskon highlights three core areas of expertise. The first is Industrial IoT and data platforms that connect industrial assets from different brands and protocols to scalable architectures. The second is AI-powered manufacturing analytics that enable anomaly detection, process optimization, and decision support in real production environments. The third is industrial pilot and demonstration projects that transform research outcomes into field-validated, market-ready solutions.

Drawing on its experience in manufacturing environments since 1997, Siskon aims to take on the roles of industrial technology provider, digital platform developer, and pilot implementation partner in European projects. The company's collaboration priorities particularly focus on topics aligned with the objectives of the European Green Deal, including energy efficiency and industrial decarbonization, industrial data spaces and interoperability, and Digital Product Passport (DPP) and CBAM compliance.

Organizations interested in exploring collaboration opportunities within Horizon Europe, Eureka, and other EU-funded R&D programmes are invited to contact the Siskon R&D team.

title: Investing in Innovation for Future Generations
excerpt: Investments in innovation ecosystems aimed at cultivating the technology leaders of the future continue to inspire young entrepreneurs and transform the sector.
author: Siskon Basın
content:
Our Open Innovation Platform: İNCİ RADAR

How Does the Process Work?

The Open Innovation Platform, İnci Radar, was launched in 2023 with the goal of expanding our companies’ entrepreneurship activities across national and international platforms and identifying solutions to the innovation needs of group companies through collaboration with the startup ecosystem. Since its launch, the platform has achieved successful results through the process framework illustrated alongside.

In order to identify the innovation needs of the Group companies for 2023, extensive collaboration was carried out with designated contacts from the Operational Excellence (OPEX), Innovation, and Engineering departments across the Group.

As a result of scouting and bridging activities conducted in line with the identified needs, startups were selected based on their commitment to creating maximum value through sustainable and responsible investments while adhering to ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) criteria.

Some of our successful implementation examples include:

1) Through the collaboration between İnci GS Yuasa and REPG Enerji, efforts are continuing on a project that generates electricity through the recovery of waste heat within the factory. The project aims to achieve annual energy savings exceeding 189,000 kWh.

2) Through the collaboration between Yusen Logistics and Siskon, an automated labeling machine project was developed. The automation solution has helped prevent human errors and delivered labor cost savings equivalent to approximately 27 personnel, thanks to increased operational speed and efficiency.

3) Through the collaboration between Maxion Aluminum and İztek Inc., an R&D project was launched to recover metal from pressed slag and reduce metal losses. By recovering approximately 30% of the aluminum contained in slag, the project is expected to prevent nearly 80 tons of metal loss.

Source: İnci RADAR

title: The latest 5G innovations will come together at the fair.
excerpt: 5G technologies and products from around the world are coming together for the first time at this year's fair, alongside the industry's leading players.
author: Siskon Basın
content:
Hannover Fairs Turkey’in 12 – 15 Mart 2020 tarihlerinde düzenleyeceği WIN EURASIA 2020 fuarında sergilenecek Türkiye sanayisinin ilk 5G senaryoları, fuar öncesi Siemens, Mitsubishi Electric, MCS, i2i Systems, SICK, Universal Robots UR, Schunk, IQ Vizyon, Merlicon, Oppent, Siskon, Simtek ve Trio Mobil’in katıldığı imza töreniyle tanıtıldı. i2i Systems’in yeni geliştirdiği yerli ve milli 5G şebekesinin ilk defa tanıtıldığı törende, 5G Arena alanında uygulanacak “5G for Smart Manufacturing” scenarios were also demonstrated. In the “Integrated Digitalization and Industry 4.0” scenario, i2i Systems’ live 5G network was tested.

The “CodeMaster Industry 4.0 Application”, designed by MCS Group, used this network to communicate through IIoT-based technologies with a Mitsubishi Electric robot, a Schunk robotic gripper, and the Siemens MindSphere cloud solution. Within the scope of the scenario, the entire lifecycle of a product could be monitored in real time from the moment a work order was created. In another scenario utilizing i2i Systems’ domestic 5G technology and showcased in collaboration with SICK, Universal Robots UR, and Schunk, real-time interaction between humans, robots, cloud systems, and sensors was demonstrated.

Highlighting the goal of supporting joint initiatives that will contribute to the transformation of various industries through 5G technologies, Hannover Fairs Turkey Managing Director Alexander Kühnel said, “The use of a domestic and national 5G frequency in integrated 5G scenarios shows that Turkey takes its National Technology Initiative seriously. At WIN EURASIA, we will bring together live 5G scenarios covering a wide range of topics, from autonomous systems and human-robot interaction to real-time heat mapping and production tracking, from dark factories and artificial intelligence to deep learning and cloud systems.”

Schunk Turkey and Middle East Country Manager Emre Sönmez stated, “In the IoT era, we integrate into systems that enhance efficiency with our products, where condition monitoring, process monitoring, and communication are carried out directly at the component level. We are excitedly anticipating the increase in commercial capacity that 5G applications will bring to our lives, especially in manufacturing environments where they will enable greater flexibility, speed, and productivity.”

ENOSAD Vice President Dr. Hüseyin Halıcı added, “Considering Turkey’s technological infrastructure in fields such as information technology and automation, we can say that domestic companies are, to a certain extent, ready for the transition to Industry 4.0. As ENOSAD, we believe that digitalization and the transition to Industry 4.0 should be among Turkey’s top priorities. We would like to express that we are ready to cooperate with both our national and international members in achieving this goal.”

Source: https://www.bthaber.com/5g-icin-en-yeniler-fuarda-bulusacak/

title: Türkiye will be introduced to 5G technology in the new year.
excerpt: With the 5G infrastructure scheduled to be implemented in the new year, Türkiye will step into a new era of communication characterized by ultra-fast connectivity and low latency.
author: Siskon Basın
content:
The industrial trade fair WIN EURASIA is bringing its 5G vision for Smart Manufacturing to Istanbul between March 12-15. Prior to the exhibition, where companies participating in the special 5G Arena zone will showcase their 5G scenarios in Türkiye for the first time, a cooperation ceremony was held featuring a domestically developed 5G network and base station. Speaking at the ceremony, Hannover Fairs Turkey General Manager Alexander Kühnel stated that they are closely following the digital transformation of Turkish companies and invited everyone interested in the latest technologies developed by local companies to attend WIN EURASIA 2020 at the TÜYAP Fair and Congress Center in Beylikdüzü.

The first 5G industrial scenarios of Türkiye, which were exhibited at WIN EURASIA 2020 organized by Hannover Fairs Turkey between March 12-15, 2020, were introduced during a signing ceremony attended by Siemens, Mitsubishi Electric, MCS, i2i Systems, SICK, Universal Robots UR, Schunk, IQ Vizyon, Merlicon, Oppent, Siskon, Simtek, and Trio Mobil.

During the ceremony, where i2i Systems announced its newly developed domestic 5G network for the first time, the “5G for Smart Manufacturing” scenarios to be implemented in the 5G Arena were presented. Within the “Integrated Digitalization and Industry 4.0” scenario, the live 5G network developed by i2i Systems was successfully tested.

The “CodeMaster Industry 4.0 Application,” designed by MCS Group, used this network to establish IIoT-based communication between a Mitsubishi Electric robot, a Schunk robotic gripper, and the Siemens MindSphere cloud solution. As part of the scenario, the entire lifecycle of a product could be monitored in real time from the moment a work order was issued.

In another scenario utilizing i2i Systems’ domestic 5G technology and exhibited in cooperation with SICK, Universal Robots UR, and Schunk, real-time interaction between humans, robots, cloud systems, and sensors was demonstrated.

Stating that the collaboration aims to encourage joint efforts that will contribute to the transformation of various industries through 5G technologies, Hannover Fairs Turkey General Manager Alexander Kühnel said:

“Türkiye is making a major leap in digital transformation. The use of a domestic 5G frequency in integrated 5G scenarios demonstrates that Türkiye takes its National Technology Initiative seriously and is opening the door to a new era. At WIN EURASIA, we will bring together live 5G scenarios covering autonomous systems, human-robot interaction, real-time heat mapping, production monitoring, dark factories, artificial intelligence, deep learning, and cloud systems. The world will witness Türkiye’s industrial strength.”

“5G Applications Will Significantly Increase Productivity”

Emre Sönmez, Country Manager for Türkiye and the Middle East at Schunk, stated that they were pleased to be part of 5G applications that will provide the speed required for Industry 4.0 technologies.

“In this era of the Internet of Things, our products enable direct status monitoring, process monitoring, and communication at the component level. By integrating into this ecosystem, we are contributing to increased efficiency. We are excited about the growth in commercial capacity that 5G applications will bring, especially in manufacturing environments where flexibility, speed, and productivity gains are essential.”

“Transition to Industry 4.0 Should Be a Priority for Türkiye”

Dr. Hüseyin Halıcı, Vice President of ENOSAD, emphasized the importance of digitalization, Industry 4.0, and domestic technology:

“Digitalization and the transition to Industry 4.0 have become more critical than ever for every branch of Turkish industry. We believe that industrial companies, particularly SMEs, will gain significant competitive advantages by adopting these technologies in production without delay. Considering Türkiye’s technological infrastructure, especially in fields such as information technologies and automation, local companies are already prepared to make substantial progress toward Industry 4.0. As ENOSAD, we believe that digitalization and Industry 4.0 should be among Türkiye’s top priorities, and we are ready to cooperate with both national and international members to contribute to this goal. We invite everyone who wishes to follow the latest developments in Industry 4.0 and digitalization to visit WIN EURASIA.”
